suitability_reason: Only decided issue (EIC eligibility) turned on the court finding petitioner's testimony about her street-vending earned income not credible and unsubstantiated; no mechanical test decided.

taxpayer.notes: Self-employed street vendor in New York, NY (socks, T-shirts, hats); cash business, no inventory or sales records; claimed EIC with two qualifying children (per fn. 3 maximum credit for two children equals amounts claimed). Filing status not stated.

adjustments: notices dated April 22 and October 17, 2016; disallowed earned income tax credit (other adjustments resolved by concessions, not described)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Eligibility for the earned income tax credit for 2014 and 2015; also claimed a constitutional right to a refund
conceded: unspecified concessions ('After concessions'); not described in opinion

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner was self-employed as a street vendor in New York, NY during 2014 and 2015
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner was self-employed as a street vendor in New York, New York, during 2014 and 2015.

findings_of_fact.fact: Customers paid mostly cash; she rarely recorded sales and gave no receipts
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner's customers usually paid her in cash, and she rarely recorded sales.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2014 Schedule C: gross receipts $16,889, expenses $1,355, net profit $15,534
findings_of_fact.snippet: On her 2014 Schedule C petitioner reported gross sales receipts of $16,889, business expenses of $1,355, and a net profit of $15,534.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2015 Schedule C: gross receipts $17,110, no expenses, net profit $17,110
findings_of_fact.snippet: On her 2015 Schedule C she reported gross sales receipts of $17,110, no business expenses, and a net profit of $17,110.
Petitioner claimed that she was eligible for an earned income tax credit of $5,460 for 2014 and $5,548 for 2015.

findings_of_fact.fact: Only documents provided to IRS were six 2014 purchase receipts totaling $1,612.25 ($355, $250, $156, $350, $400, $101.25)
findings_of_fact.snippet: six receipts (totaling $1,612.252) for items she purchased for resale during 2014.

findings_of_fact.fact: Maximum EIC for an eligible individual with two qualifying children was $5,460 (2014) and $5,548 (2015)
findings_of_fact.snippet: The largest earned income tax credit for an eligible individual with two qualifying children was $5,460 for 2014 and $5,548 for 2015.

findings_of_fact.fact: Bank account closed in 2016 and records discarded; no bank records offered
findings_of_fact.snippet: she testified that she closed the account at some point in 2016 and discarded all of her bank records.

findings_of_fact.fact: Court found testimony on income and expenses not credible; earned income not established
findings_of_fact.snippet: Thus, petitioner has not established the amount of her earned income for 2014 and 2015

issues.question: Is petitioner eligible for the earned income tax credit for 2014 or 2015?
issues.holding: Not eligible: petitioner did not establish the amount of her earned income; testimony not credible and no records
issues.computable_reason: Decided on credibility/substantiation of earned income; no found earned-income figure to compute the credit from

decision.text: Decisions will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: EIC denied for 2014 and 2015; no refund right; Rule 155 computation after concessions

notes: Consolidated dockets 11326-16S and 25317-16S (consolidated Dec. 11, 2017). Some facts stipulated. Burden on petitioner (sec. 7491 not invoked). Footnote marker '2' fused to receipts total in text ('$1,612.252' = $1,612.25 + fn 2). Number of qualifying children not stated directly; fn. 3 implies two.
